# Corner Loaf Bakery — online ordering Customers order on the website and pay when they pick up. Staff see orders on `/admin`. Built with Python's standard library only: no packages to install. ## Run it ```sh python3 -m bakery.server --port 8000 --db data/bakery.db ``` Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The admin page is http://127.0.0.1:8000/admin; the username can be anything, and the password is `ADMIN_PASSWORD` (default `flour`). The database file is created and seeded with the menu and promo codes on first start. `data/bakery.db` is the live database, with real customer orders in it. Don't delete it. ## Test it ```sh python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v ``` Each test starts the server on a free port with a throwaway database. Set `CORNERLOAF_NOW=2026-10-08T09:10:00` (store local time) to pin the clock; the tests do this. ## How it fits together | File | What it does | |---|---| | `bakery/server.py` | Routes, order validation, HTML pages, admin | | `bakery/db.py` | SQLite schema, seed menu and promo codes, queries | | `bakery/pricing.py` | Subtotal, promo discount, sales tax and total | | `bakery/clock.py` | Store-local "now" (pinnable for tests) | | `bakery/templates/` | Page templates (`string.Template`) | | `bakery/static/` | CSS, cart (localStorage) and checkout script | ## API The checkout page and the bookkeeper's export both use this API. Keep existing fields and status codes working when you change things; add new fields rather than renaming old ones. - `GET /api/menu` → `{"products": [{"sku", "name", "price", "category"}]}` - `POST /api/orders` with `{"customer": {"name", "email", "phone"}, "pickup_date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "items": [{"sku", "qty"}], "promo_code"}` → `201` and the order. Invalid input → `400 {"error": "..."}`. - `GET /api/orders/` → the order, or `404`. - `GET /admin/api/orders[?date=YYYY-MM-DD]` (admin) → `{"orders": [...]}`. - `POST /admin/api/orders//cancel` (admin) → the order, with `status` `"cancelled"`. An order looks like: ```json {"id": 1, "status": "placed", "created_at": "2026-10-08T09:10:00", "customer": {"name": "Ana", "email": "ana@example.com", "phone": "555-0100"}, "pickup_date": "2026-10-10", "items": [{"sku": "BREAD9", "name": "Sourdough Loaf", "qty": 2, "unit_price": 9.0, "line_total": 18.0}], "promo_code": null, "subtotal": 18.0, "discount": 0.0, "tax": 1.44, "total": 19.44} ``` Money in the API is dollars as JSON numbers with at most two decimals. Admin endpoints use HTTP Basic auth; they return `401` without it. # Tax is wrong when people use a coupon A customer emailed to say we charged her sales tax on the full price even though she used a coupon. My bookkeeper says tax should only be on what people actually pay for food, after the coupon. Gift cards shouldn't be taxed at all, and coupons are for food, not gift cards. She also says that when it comes to half a cent, we always round up. # Let people choose a pickup time Saturday mornings are chaos: everyone shows up at 9. When people order, I want them to choose a half-hour pickup time while we're open. We can handle 4 orders in each half hour. We need at least 2 hours to get an order ready, and birthday cakes and catering trays need 2 days because we bake them to order. On the orders page, show me the pickup times and list the orders in the order I'll be handing them out. # Stop selling more than we can bake Last Saturday we sold nine birthday cakes and I can only make six a day. I spent Friday night calling people to apologise. Each day we can make 6 birthday cakes, 4 catering trays and 8 seasonal pies. We can keep up with everything else. Don't let anyone order more than that, and tell them it's sold out. # Let people spend gift cards online People buy gift cards on the site, but there's no way to spend them online. They have to bring the card in. When someone buys a gift card, give them a gift card code on their order page. At checkout, let people enter a code to pay with it. If the card has more on it than the order, keep the rest for next time. Show them how much came off the card and what's left. # Let customers cancel online Customers keep calling to cancel, and I can't always answer the phone. Let them cancel from the page they see after ordering. Not on the day of pickup, though, because by then we've already baked it. # Show what's sold out before people fill their cart People pick a day, fill their cart and only find out at checkout that the cakes are gone. When someone is choosing what to order, let them pick the day they're coming and show what's already sold out for that day, so they can't add it. # Let people change their cart If someone adds three loaves by mistake, the only fix is to start over. At checkout, let people change how many of each thing they want, or take something out, before they order. # Show the total before they order People don't see what they'll pay until after they've ordered. On the checkout page, show the total with any coupon and gift card taken off, and what they'll still owe at pickup, before they press the button. It has to match what we actually charge.
